title: Succinct Arguments for QMA from Collapsing Hash Functions
abstract: We prove the existence of succinct arguments for QMA, assuming only the existence of collapsing hash functions. This is the first scheme that relies only on unstructured ``Minicrypt'' assumptions, which are not known to imply public-key encryption.   Our main technical contribution is a quantum-succinct \emph{claw-state generation} protocol that allows us to bootstrap a small number of quantum correlations into an arbitrarily large number of claw-state correlations, using classical communication only. This improves upon the work of [Zhang, STOC 2021], having better round complexity, a proof in the standard model, and being overall much simpler. This yields a quantum-succinct blind delegation of quantum computation protocol from one-way functions, which we plug into the communication-compression compiler of [Bartusek, Liu, and Malavolta, EUROCRYPT 2026] to obtain succinct arguments for QMA.
summary: This paper establishes a method to create succinct arguments for QMA, the quantum analogue of NP, relying only on the assumption of collapsing hash functions. The key technical breakthrough is a quantum-succinct protocol for generating claw states, which is then integrated into a compiler to yield the final result. This advances the field by placing QMA verification in the 'Minicrypt' complexity class.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the existence of succinct arguments for QMA (Quantum Merlin-Arthur) using only unstructured cryptographic assumptions.
main_result: They prove this existence assuming only the existence of collapsing hash functions, yielding a quantum-succinct blind delegation of quantum computation protocol.
method: The core method involves constructing a quantum-succinct claw-state generation protocol and combining it with a communication-compression compiler to achieve the final argument system.
model_or_system: The work is purely theoretical, dealing with computational complexity classes (QMA) and cryptographic primitives (collapsing hash functions, one-way functions).
key_observables: Soundness error, completeness probability, communication complexity, and verifier runtime bounds.
important_parameters: The security relies on the existence of collapsing hash functions and the complexity parameters $\lambda$ (security parameter) and $\epsilon$ (error tolerance).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the existence of 'collapsing hash functions,' which are unstructured cryptographic primitives, placing the result in the 'Minicrypt' model.
paper_structure: The structure builds from the general problem of succinct arguments for QMA, introduces the necessary technical tool—the quantum-succinct claw-state generation protocol—and finally combines this with established compilation techniques to yield the main theorem.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, advancements in quantum verification protocols and complexity theory underpin the fundamental limits of what quantum computation can be proven efficiently, which is relevant to understanding quantum information processing capabilities.
